channel_name: Fleet Select and Fleet Building Experience

messages.content:
There's some room for improvement on the Neb experience. I'd be curious to hear people's thoughts on what they think would be a big improvement

A few examples:
- searchable metadata tags to fleets (missiles, caps) 
- making fleets searchable by hulls.
- easy renaming/duplicating/versioning of fleets
- sorting fleets by last modified/used/created date
- in-game editable fleet/missile descriptions and a fleetbuilding notes

Here is a (poor) mockup of what some of that could look like, but I'd be interested to hear people's thoughts.

Question: What default tags make sense?
There are some default describers: I have frontline, caps, skirmish, backline as fleet roles

I'm also thinking of automatically assigning tags if fleets meet certain criteria. Some options:
- missile (auto if over 500 pts of munitions in a fleet)
- rails (auto if md/rail mounts)
- cv (auto if cv hull in fleet if it's something cringe you'll deal)
Autoapplying things like caps gets a little sus with sprinterballs etc, I'd only add in a button that goes through fleets and applies selected tags based on criteria 

But overall, if you could add a few basic broadly applicable tags, what would they be?
caps can be done if they're running 6+ sprinters outside of formation
intel if Intel center

Frontline, Blob (or skirmish mabye as an alternative word for this so CLs aren't just lumped into frontline?), Caps, Artillery, Ambush, DIRECT, YUB, CV
Honestly those'd probably be the only tags I'd use when finding a fleet
Also, I'd favor manually assigned tags instead of trying to auto-generate them (or an option to toggle between manual and automatic tagging)
it would be cool to have an option to sort by game version, if that can be pulled from the fleet file itself or extrapolated from the last date modified and a internal table of balance changes

These seem pretty good, although I'd suggest for the autogenerated tags, excluding BF/BF-EL missiles from the count for the total amount of points invested in missiles so a pure ASF escort carrier with a SAMfrig, or John ACM doesn't get assigned the missile tag

Within this is a question of where should I step back from auto labeling fleets and let users drive them.
Auto labeling is intended as a convenience/onboarding rather than enforcing convention.
A few broad clear indisputable labels are better than full edge case ones.
i think the ability to autogen and then allow users to remove them with a single click, and make it user configureable would be good
Yeah, this would be a good compromise between autogenerated and user selected

I should have a little time this weekend to work on this (and maybe even play the game a little), so other general feedback before then is good. I'll put a few open questions here for folks to give opinions on:

**Search/sort behavior:** should it ignore folders and just give you an absolute list?
For example if I sort by most recently modified, I can list out top to bottom the most recent fleets I worked on. But nebulous search now is built around finding matches inside of folders. 
Should sort keep folders 👍 or transform into a flat list 👎?

**Liner hull reroll/defaults:**
I'm adding a little bit of the mod into shipbuilding to let you set tags, so I thought I'd maybe address a common annoyance. Should I toss in the ability to generate a "correct" (back thrusters etc) liner format as part of drydock?
**Fleet modification**: Do people want more menu options to rename/copy/versioning of fleets? I'm not sure if the versioning is really useful for most players, and copy is mostly resave
I'll take whatever you give us ngl. I have no reference for how much work any of this is or how achievable it is.

Beamstone without FPAs
RCC => ANS using RCC => ANS guns do not benefit, use ammo elevators to buff guns
No secondary antenna on BB => BB must have secondary antenna => the built in antenna dies incredibly frequently, mounts 6/7/10/11 are recommended to mount a replacement.

If folks put together a clear list of 40 or so traps/reqs I'll look into per compartment fleetbuilding scanning and alerting.
Let's keep format as 

Situation => Rule => Reason

Example:
ANS Mk600 Beam Cannon and Mk610 Beam Turret => Requires 2+ Focused Particle Accelerator => Beams deal many small ticks of damage and FPAs are needed to boost the damage above the threshold required to break reinforced components
Mm. Magazine/CIC in the center stack of a CL => Present in comps 1-4 => most incoming damage to CLs ends up there, relocate critical components to the nose or rear where they are safer

Ship with large compartments (including ANS carriers) => Ship with non-large compartments/magazines in the large compartments => non-magazine compartments do not scale with compartment size and are therefore fragile. Use large compartment specific equipment intended to be placed in these slots.
Small drives in big drive slot => same as above
Carrier with repair station => Do not add repair stations to carrier hulls => carriers come with a repair station built into the hull
Using the Strobe correlator => do not use the strobe correlator => this module is currently useless
Using the signature scrambler => do not use the signature Scrambler => this module is currently useless
Using more than two ARR => Radars do not benefit from more than one ARR => This radar has already been buffed to the noise floor, further ARRs will have no effect
Power drive in a liner => don't use power drive on a Frontline hull=> This will significantly affect the liner's ability to maneuver and aim.

CLN with anything that is not a container launcher or bank hangar in it's big slots => Do not use CLN for things other than it is intended => what you are doing is bad and has made god very unhappy. The purpose of this backline hull is to bring specialized equipment that OSP otherwise struggles to bring; container missiles en mass and craft en mass. To do otherwise is a waste, use a hull more fitting for what you are trying to do.

ANS ship with no RPF despite eligible guns => bring RPF => ANS light guns are balanced around their access to RPF; without this round they will be at significant disadvantage against OSP light ships, and unable to perform the tasks handed to them as a dual purpose turret.
450 ship with no HE => 450 ships must bring 450 HE => 450 HE is useful for engaging broadside capitals/and Liners as well as anything smaller.
450 ship with no AP => 450 ships must bring 450 AP => 450 AP is useful for engaging bow-on capitals and punching through stacks of reinforced components

Less than 3 restores on an Ocello/Axford, 6 on a battleship, 2 on a CL, 6 on a Liner => These hulls should have x restores or greater. Exceptions for rail gun/mass driver ships => restores are necessary to maintain combat power throughout the match
Railguns on a BB
BBs have a significant hull debuff to rails, consider bringing a rail CH or rail DDs
Guns in backpack mounts on ANS hulls
Broad siding makes you an easier target than bowtanking, while reducing the effects of armor angling
Ship without chaff =>  chaff on ship => ships rely on chaff for defense against cruise missiles

Thanks. Try to keep each line clearly contained with all three pieces (situation, rule, reason) so that I'm not hunting around. 
The reason is important bc some stuff is self-evident if you know the game, but the main benefactors of this would be people that might not know obvious stuff
Be pretty explicit too

Flares present on ship => Ships with a coms jammer should not carry flares => the only use of flares as a decoy is against CMD/WAKE, as they have no effect on validators. Without a coms jammer, the flares will not be useful.
OSP 250 Ship with no Bombshell => Bring bombshell => OSP needs bombshell to fire on craft, missiles, and groups of light ships under jamming.

OSP ship with no Grapeshot despite eligible guns => bring Grapeshot => OSP light guns are balanced around their access to Grapeshot; without this round they will be at significant disadvantage against ANS light ships, and unable to perform the tasks handed to them as a dual purpose turret.

Both plasma and 100mm weapons present on ship => use 100mm HE-HC => 100mm HE-HC cannot pen ANS without the use of plasma, but once targets have been armor stripped, it allows OSP to deliver massive damage.

Using the Supplementary Radio Amplifier => Do not use on ship without CR70/CR75 antenna => The SRA allows a ship's command missiles to punch deeper into defensive coms jamming, making them harder to softkill.
Small Reactor Booster => only use this module in small module slots =>  if present in a larger slot, use the micro reactor instead
Mount Gyros => Don't use on ships other than Beam Axford or Solomon => Use this module to buff the Beam Turret

Damage Control Central => If fewer than 7 DC Teams and rapid teams, Don't use DC buff compartments => As a buff compartment, this compartment does nothing on its own and only becomes worth using when you have x number of teams

Small Workshop => If fewer than 7 DC Teams and rapid teams, Don't use DC buff compartments => As a buff compartment, this compartment does nothing on its own and only becomes worth using when you have x number of teams
RDC/DCX => Capitals without Reinforced Damage Control/DCX => Capitals require RDC/DCX to survive and recover from strikes

Light assets with reinforced CIC/Damage control => Don't use reinforced damage control or CICs on light ships => These ships do not have enough damage reduction to keep these reinforced components alive under light gunfire or missile strikes.
Sprinter without Aux Steering => Sprinters should have an Aux steering => Aux steering allows sprinters to survive under fire to capture points, albeit without offensive capability

Keystone with Aux Steering => Keystones should not have aux steerings with only a single CIC => The Keystone does not benefit you when becoming a cringe capper more than it would staying combat capable with a 2nd CIC

Reinforced Drives => Reinforced Drives on Capitals => The only benefit these drives bring over other drives is requiring large caliber HE to kill. The ship would benefit more not being hit in the first place
Acceleration Drives => Capital ships require an acceleration drive (Raider, Yard/7700) => These ships accelerate slowly and struggle to reach top speed, change directions, or dodge fire without one.
